/-!
# Erdős Problem 966

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/966](https://www.erdosproblems.com/966)
- [Er75b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Journées
  Arithmétiques de Bordeaux (Conf., Univ. Bordeaux, Bordeaux, 1974) (1975), 295-310.
-/

namespace Erdos966

/--
Let $k,r\geq 2$. Does there exist a set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that contains no non-trivial
arithmetic progression of length $k+1$, yet in any $r$-colouring of $A$ there must exist a
monochromatic non-trivial arithmetic progression of length $k$?

Erdős [Er75b] reported that 'Spencer has recently shown that such a sequence exists', but gives
no reference.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos966.lean"]
theorem erdos_966 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ k r : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → 2 ≤ r → ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.IsAPOfLengthFree (k + 1) ∧
      ∀ coloring : A → Fin r, ContainsMonoAPofLength coloring k := by
  sorry

end Erdos966

reformulations.difference: Nontrivial progressions are encoded by exact ENat cardinality rather than an explicit positive common difference. The declaration also quantifies over colourings of A, whereas the linked formal proof quantifies over colourings of all of ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For m ≥ 2, s.IsAPOfLengthWith m a d is equivalent to 0 < d together with s = {a + i*d : i < m}. A zero step produces a singleton, contradicting cardinality m; a positive step gives an injective enumeration with exactly m elements. Thus IsAPOfLengthFree and ContainsMonoAPofLength have the required nontrivial-progression meanings. Since r ≥ 2, any colouring of A extends to ℕ using a default colour, and global colourings restrict to A. The full equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, and the bridge from the linked proof to the exact repository statement was checked in /workspace/review/fullcheck.lean.
